📖 Introduction to ICT Trading

ICT methodology is based on understanding how institutional traders (banks, hedge funds, central banks) move price. Markets are driven by the IPDA algorithm that seeks liquidity and delivers price to the next pool.

Core Premise: Markets are NOT random. They are driven by an algorithm (IPDA — Interbank Price Delivery Algorithm) that seeks out liquidity (stop losses) and delivers price to the next liquidity pool.

5 Key Principles:
1. Price seeks liquidity — always moves toward clusters of stop losses
2. Imbalances get filled — FVGs and gaps are magnets for future price
3. Smart money leaves footprints — Order Blocks show where institutions traded
4. Time is a factor — specific sessions have specific behaviors
5. Higher timeframes dominate — always trade with the HTF bias

Who is ICT? Michael J. Huddleston, a professional trader who reverse-engineered how institutional money moves in forex and commodities markets. His methodology is used by thousands of professional traders worldwide.

📊 Market Structure — The Foundation

Market structure is the backbone of ICT trading. Bullish = higher highs and higher lows. Bearish = lower lows and lower highs. BOS = trend continuation. CHoCH = first warning of reversal.

Bullish Structure: Series of Higher Highs (HH) and Higher Lows (HL). Each swing high breaks the previous. Each pullback holds above the previous HL. Trade: enter on pullbacks to OBs/FVGs in the discount zone.

Bearish Structure: Series of Lower Lows (LL) and Lower Highs (LH). Each swing low breaks the previous. Each rally fails below the previous LH. Trade: enter on rallies to OBs/FVGs in the premium zone.

BOS — Break of Structure: Price breaks the last swing high/low IN the direction of the trend. This is a continuation signal — the trend is healthy. Do NOT fade BOS.

CHoCH — Change of Character: Price breaks structure AGAINST the current trend. This is the FIRST warning of a reversal. One CHoCH alone is not enough — wait for confirmation with a liquidity sweep.

Swing Points: The bot uses the last 4 swing highs and 4 swing lows to determine structure. A swing high requires at least 2 lower highs on each side. A swing low requires at least 2 higher lows on each side.

Pro tip: Always identify structure on the H4/Daily first, then drill down to H1/M15 for entry. Never trade M5 structure against H4 structure.

⚡ Fair Value Gaps (FVG) — ICT's Most Powerful Tool

A Fair Value Gap is a 3-candle imbalance where price moved so fast only one side of the market traded. It acts like a magnet, drawing price back to fill the gap. 68% of FVGs fill within 24 hours.

How to Identify a Bullish FVG:
Candle 1: Any candle — note its HIGH
Candle 2: A displacement/expansion candle
Candle 3: A candle whose LOW is ABOVE Candle 1's HIGH
The FVG zone = between Candle 1 HIGH and Candle 3 LOW

How to Identify a Bearish FVG:
Candle 1: Any candle — note its LOW
Candle 2: A displacement candle
Candle 3: A candle whose HIGH is BELOW Candle 1's LOW
The FVG zone = between Candle 3 HIGH and Candle 1 LOW

4 Types of FVGs:
1. Standard FVG — the classic 3-candle imbalance
2. Implied FVG — smaller, requires a microscope view on M1/M5
3. Inverse FVG (IFVG) — a FILLED FVG that now acts as support/resistance
4. NW Gap (No Wick Gap) — no overlapping wicks at all — the STRONGEST type

Consequent Encroachment (CE): The 50% level of the FVG. This is the most magnetic point within the gap — price often stalls or reverses exactly at CE.

Gold FVG Statistics:
• 68% of FVGs get at least 50% filled within 24 hours
• 45% get fully filled within 48 hours
• FVGs created during London/NY kill zones have higher fill rates
• HTF-aligned FVGs have a 72% fill rate

Entry using FVG: Wait for price to return TO the FVG zone. Enter at the CE (50%) or at the FVG boundary. Stop loss below the FVG low (for buys) or above the FVG high (for sells).

🏛️ Order Blocks — Institutional Footprints

An Order Block is the last opposing candle before a significant directional move — it shows exactly where institutions placed their orders. Bullish OB: last bearish candle before a bullish impulse. Bearish OB: last bullish candle before a bearish impulse.

Bullish Order Block:
Pattern: [Bearish candle] → [Strong bullish expansion]
The last bearish candle before the bullish move IS the OB
It acts as support — price returns here to allow more buying

Bearish Order Block:
Pattern: [Bullish candle] → [Strong bearish expansion]
The last bullish candle before the bearish move IS the OB
It acts as resistance — price returns here to allow more selling

5 OB Quality Factors (scored 1-5):
1. Displacement strength — bigger expansion candle = stronger OB
2. Volume at creation — higher volume = institutional signature
3. Distance from price — OBs closer to current price are more relevant
4. HTF alignment — H4/Daily OBs are far stronger than H1 OBs
5. Zone freshness — the FIRST touch of an OB is most powerful

Entry Technique:
• Wait for price to RETURN to the OB zone
• Look for confirmation: FVG within OB, or a rejection candle at the OB
• Enter at OB midpoint (50% level)
• Stop loss BELOW the OB low (for buys) or ABOVE the OB high (for sells)

Breaker Blocks: When an Order Block FAILS (price breaks through it), it flips polarity and becomes a Breaker Block — now acting as resistance (former bull OB) or support (former bear OB). These are extremely high-probability zones because retail traders are still long/short from the original OB.

🕐 Kill Zones & Silver Bullet Windows

Kill Zones are the only times worth trading. Outside these windows, the market is manipulated or ranging. Asian: 00:00–03:00 UTC. London: 07:00–10:00 UTC. New York: 13:00–16:00 UTC. Silver Bullet: 10:00–11:00 UTC.

Why Kill Zones matter: Institutional orders are executed at specific times of day. Outside kill zones, price is often engineered to trap retail traders. Trading ONLY during kill zones dramatically improves win rate.

Asian Session (00:00–03:00 UTC / 02:00–05:00 SAST):
• Low volatility — accumulation phase
• Establishes the Asia range (high and low)
• The Asia range often gets swept during London open (Judas Swing)
• Avoid trading during this session

London Kill Zone (07:00–10:00 UTC / 09:00–12:00 SAST):
• Highest volume session for Gold
• Judas Swing often occurs: price sweeps Asia range then reverses violently
• Best FVG/OB setups form here
• Bot uses this as primary entry window

New York Kill Zone (13:00–16:00 UTC / 15:00–18:00 SAST):
• Second-highest volume
• Often continues or reverses the London move
• NY Open at 13:30 UTC causes the biggest moves
• NFP/CPI/FOMC releases happen during NY hours

🥇 Silver Bullet (10:00–11:00 UTC / 12:00–13:00 SAST):
ICT's highest-probability daily setup window.
5-Step Silver Bullet Model:
1. Kill zone active (London-NY overlap or NY open)
2. Liquidity sweep occurs (stop hunt above/below recent swing)
3. Market Structure Shift (MSS) — price reverses and breaks structure
4. FVG created on M1 chart during the displacement
5. Enter on FVG retest, target previous session high/low

The bot scores +2 when Silver Bullet is active (1 for KZ active, 1 bonus for SB specifically).

💧 Liquidity — How Smart Money Hunts Stops

Liquidity is clusters of stop losses sitting above swing highs (BSL) or below swing lows (SSL). Smart money NEEDS this liquidity to fill large institutional orders. They engineer price to trigger these stops, then reverse.

Two types of liquidity:
• BSL (Buy-Side Liquidity): Stop losses of SHORT sellers, sitting ABOVE swing highs
• SSL (Sell-Side Liquidity): Stop losses of LONG buyers, sitting BELOW swing lows

The Hunt Pattern:
1. Price slowly approaches a liquidity pool (swing high or low)
2. Price breaks above/below it — triggering retail stop losses
3. Price IMMEDIATELY reverses — this is your entry signal
4. Smart money has now filled their orders and drives price the other way

Equal Highs/Lows: When price makes two or more highs/lows at the SAME level, this is a massive liquidity magnet. Retail traders place stops just above/below these levels. Smart money WILL target them.

ICT Rule #1 (CallistoFX): NO LIQUIDITY SWEEP = NO TRADE. If price hasn't swept a significant high or low before your setup, the trade has no institutional backing. Wait.

Stop Hunt vs Genuine Breakout:
• Stop hunt: breaks the level then CLOSES BACK inside it on same candle
• Genuine breakout: closes above/below AND stays there with follow-through
• The wick above/below but close inside = classic stop hunt signal

Inducement: ICT concept where price creates a small, obvious swing high/low to LURE retail traders into a position — only to sweep their stops and continue the real move.

📐 Premium & Discount Zones — Where to Buy and Sell

Premium = above the 50% equilibrium of a price range. Discount = below. ICT Rule: BUY in discount, SELL in premium. Never buy at the top of a range or sell at the bottom.

The Fibonacci Connection:
ICT uses the 50% level (equilibrium) as the key dividing line between premium and discount.

Price Zones:
• 0–25%: Extreme Discount — highest probability BUY zone
• 25–50%: Discount — acceptable BUY zone
• 50%: Equilibrium — neutral, wait for confirmation
• 50–75%: Premium — acceptable SELL zone
• 75–100%: Extreme Premium — highest probability SELL zone

OTE — Optimal Trade Entry (61.8%–79%):
The golden zone for ICT entries. When price retraces into the 61.8%–79% Fibonacci level of a previous swing AND aligns with an OB or FVG, this is the OTE — the highest probability entry point ICT offers.

Practical Application:
1. Identify the last major swing high and swing low
2. If bullish: only look to BUY when price is below the 50% level
3. If bearish: only look to SELL when price is above the 50% level
4. The bot checks P/D on every signal — adds 1 point if P/D is correct

Common Mistake: Buying at the top of a range (premium) because 'it looks bullish.' This is exactly where smart money is SELLING to retail longs.

⚡ Power of 3 — AMD Model

Power of 3 is ICT's framework for understanding every trading day. Accumulation (Asia = build position), Manipulation (London open = Judas Swing traps retail), Distribution (NY = true move direction).

The 3 Phases Every Day:

Phase 1 — Accumulation (Asia Session):
• Institutions quietly build their position
• Price ranges tightly — the Asia range forms
• Retail traders see 'nothing happening' and either ignore it or get trapped in ranges

Phase 2 — Manipulation (London Open):
• This is the FAKE move — the Judas Swing
• Price breaks OUT of the Asia range in the WRONG direction
• Retail traders chase the breakout and get trapped
• Their stop losses are now fuel for Phase 3

Phase 3 — Distribution (New York Session):
• The TRUE directional move begins
• Price reverses aggressively from the Judas Swing high/low
• Sweeps Asia range in the opposite direction
• This is where the big moves happen and where the bot looks to trade

Judas Swing Pattern:
• Price breaks above Asia high → expect bearish reversal
• Price breaks below Asia low → expect bullish reversal
• The wick above/below Asia range IS the Judas Swing
• Entry: wait for MSS after the sweep, then FVG/OB entry

Daily Range Target: After Phase 2 sweep, the distribution target is usually the OPPOSITE extreme of the Asia range. E.g. if price Judas Swings above Asia high, target is below Asia low.

🌅 NDOG & NWOG — Opening Gaps

NDOG (New Day Opening Gap) and NWOG (New Week Opening Gap) are powerful magnetic price levels. They form when price gaps at the daily or weekly open and must be filled.

NDOG — New Day Opening Gap:
Forms between 5PM NY close (22:00 UTC) and 6PM NY reopen (23:00 UTC)
• A gap forms if today's open ≠ yesterday's close
• Acts as a magnet — price is drawn back to fill it
• Can use as TP target or as an entry zone
• Most reliable during London and NY kill zones

NWOG — New Week Opening Gap:
Forms between Friday 5PM close and Sunday 5PM open
• Weekend news and positioning creates gaps
• Very strong magnet — 80%+ of weekly gaps fill within the week
• Monday London open often moves directly to fill the NWOG

How to Trade Gaps:
1. Identify the gap zone (between Friday close and Monday open)
2. Wait for price to approach the gap from the opposite direction
3. Look for an OB or FVG confluence AT the gap level
4. Enter with gap fill as your TP1, then let the runner extend

CE of the Gap: The 50% midpoint of the gap is the most magnetic level — price often stalls exactly here before deciding to fully fill or reverse.

🎯 HTF Bias — Top-Down Analysis

Higher Timeframe bias determines which direction you're allowed to trade. Daily → H4 → H1 → M15. Never take a trade against the D1 or H4 trend. The HTF is always right.

Top-Down Analysis Process:
1. Start on Daily chart — what is the overall trend?
2. Drop to H4 — is it confirming the Daily bias?
3. Drop to H1 — find the kill zone setup
4. Drop to M15/M5 — fine-tune the entry
5. Never skip steps — going straight to M5 is retail thinking

HTF Bias Rules:
• If D1 is bearish → ONLY take short signals on H1/M15
• If H4 is bullish → only take long setups
• Counter-trend trades require 8+/10 confluence score
• When D1 and H4 disagree → sit out, wait for alignment

EMA 8/21 for Bias:
The bot uses EMA8 and EMA21 crossover on H4 candles to determine bias:
• EMA8 > EMA21 by 0.05% → Bullish bias
• EMA8 < EMA21 by 0.05% → Bearish bias
• Within range → Neutral (bot reduces confidence score)

Gold-Specific: Gold strongly follows the DXY (US Dollar Index) in inverse. If DXY is trending up, Gold bias should be bearish. If DXY is trending down, Gold bias should be bullish. The bot now checks DXY automatically and deducts 1 point when conflict is detected.

📏 Risk Management — Protecting Your Capital

Professional ICT traders risk 0.5–1% per trade with 1:3 to 1:5 RR. One bad trade should never hurt you. One good trade shouldn't make you greedy. Consistency over big wins.

Position Sizing:
Risk Amount = Account Balance × Risk %
Lot Size = Risk Amount ÷ (SL Points × Point Value)
For Gold (GOLD#): 1 lot = $10 per point, 0.01 lot = $0.10 per point

ICT Risk Rules:
• Maximum risk per trade: 1% of account
• Maximum daily drawdown: 3–5% of account
• Stop trading after 2 consecutive losses (reset mindset)
• Never move SL further away — only to break-even or tighter
• Never add to a losing position

The 3 Trade Management Stages:
Stage 1: Entry → 1:1 profit = take 50% off (partial close). This is now built into the bot automatically.
Stage 2: Move SL to break-even + 0.10 points. Trade is now risk-free.
Stage 3: Trail SL behind price. Let the winner run to 1:3 or beyond.

Why Partial Close? Taking 50% off at 1:1 means even if the remaining 50% hits SL at break-even, you've still made money. It converts a potential loss into a guaranteed win.

Max Daily Drawdown: The bot automatically stops trading if daily drawdown exceeds your configured limit. This prevents one bad day from destroying your account.

🔄 Displacement & Momentum Candles

A displacement candle is a large, fast-moving candle with minimal wicks that shows institutional commitment. It creates FVGs, confirms OBs, and signals the start of a real directional move.

What makes a Displacement Candle:
• Body is 70%+ of the candle's total range
• Body is larger than the average of the last 10 candles
• Closes near its high (bullish) or near its low (bearish)
• Creates a FVG on the candle before or after it

Why Displacement matters:
Displacement = institutional participation. Retail traders create choppy, indecisive candles with long wicks. Institutions create clean, decisive candles that move far and fast. When you see displacement, follow it.

Displacement in the AMD Model:
• Phase 2 (Manipulation) often creates a displacement candle as the Judas Swing
• Phase 3 (Distribution) starts with a strong displacement candle after the MSS
• The FVG INSIDE the displacement candle is the prime entry zone

Aggressive Mode: In aggressive mode, the bot can enter on displacement alone (without full confluence). This captures scalp moves but requires a tight 1:2 RR and very fast execution.

🔢 Confluence — How the Bot Scores Setups

The bot scores every setup out of 10. Each ICT factor adds 1 point. Normal mode requires 7/10. Sniper mode requires 8/10. Never trade below your minimum — patience is the edge.

The 10-Point Confluence System:

1️⃣ Kill Zone active (London/NY/Silver Bullet window) → +1
2️⃣ Silver Bullet window specifically → +1 bonus
3️⃣ Fair Value Gap present in trade direction → +1
4️⃣ Order Block present in trade direction → +1
5️⃣ Market Structure Shift confirmed (BOS/CHoCH) → +1
6️⃣ Liquidity sweep occurred (CallistoFX Rule #1) → +1
7️⃣ HTF Bias aligned with trade direction → +1
8️⃣ OTE Fibonacci zone (61.8–79% retracement) → +1
9️⃣ Premium/Discount correct (buy discount, sell premium) → +1
🔟 Power of 3 / Judas Swing confirmation → +1

Deductions:
• DXY conflict detected → -1 (bot checks DXY automatically)

Mode Thresholds:
• Aggressive: 3/10 minimum — scalp mode, many trades
• Normal: 7/10 minimum — standard ICT setup
• Sniper: 8/10 minimum — only the best setups

Why patience wins: The difference between a 6/10 and an 8/10 setup is enormous. A 6/10 setup might have 45% win rate. An 8/10 setup often has 70%+. Waiting for high confluence is the single biggest edge you can have.

🌍 Gold (XAUUSD) — Specific Market Knowledge

Gold is the most predictable ICT market. It follows the DXY in inverse, respects kill zones religiously, and responds to ICT concepts more reliably than any forex pair.

Gold Characteristics:
• Spread: typically 0.25–0.50 points — very tradeable
• Volatility: 15–30 point average daily range
• Best sessions: London (07:00–10:00 UTC) and NY (13:00–16:00 UTC)
• Worst time: Asian session (00:00–07:00 UTC) — avoid

DXY Inverse Correlation:
• DXY rises → Gold falls (inverse relationship)
• DXY falls → Gold rises
• When DXY is in a strong trend, Gold follows in reverse
• The bot now tracks DXY automatically and flags conflicts

High-Impact Events for Gold:
• NFP (Non-Farm Payrolls) — first Friday of month — 30min blackout
• CPI (Consumer Price Index) — 2nd week of month — 30min blackout
• FOMC — 8 times per year — extreme volatility — sit out
• Fed Chair speeches — unpredictable spikes
• The bot auto-pauses 30 minutes before/after all these events

Gold Pip/Point Value:
• 1 lot = $10 per 1-point move
• 0.1 lot = $1 per 1-point move
• 0.01 lot = $0.10 per 1-point move (minimum — good for learning)
• A 20-point SL on 0.01 lot = $2 risk — perfect for small accounts

Gold's Personality: Gold respects Order Blocks and FVGs extremely well. It sweeps liquidity aggressively before reversing. The Power of 3 / Judas Swing pattern works on Gold almost every London open.

🧠 Trading Psychology — The Hardest Part

90% of retail traders lose. The edge of ICT concepts is real — but it means nothing without the psychological discipline to execute the plan, take losses, and not revenge trade.

The 4 Killers of Retail Traders:
1. Revenge trading — doubling down after a loss to 'get it back'
2. Widening stops — moving SL further away when price moves against you
3. Cutting winners early — closing at 1:1 when 1:3 was the target
4. FOMO — entering a trade because price is moving without you

Why the Bot Helps:
The bot removes emotion from the equation. It doesn't revenge trade. It doesn't widen stops. It follows the plan every time. This is why automated or semi-automated trading outperforms manual trading for most people.

Rules to Live By:
• A setup that doesn't meet minimum confluence score is NOT a setup — it's a gamble
• If you've hit your daily drawdown limit — STOP. The market will be there tomorrow.
• 3 losses in a row = take the day off. Something is wrong with the session.
• Profits are not yours until they're withdrawn. Book partial profits regularly.

Journaling:
Write down every trade: entry reason, confluence score, outcome, what you learned. After 50 trades you'll see patterns in your mistakes. This is how professionals improve.

Backtesting: The History tab shows your bot's performance. Review it weekly. If win rate drops below 45% — review your confluence settings. If it's above 65% — you've found your edge.

⚙️ Bot Modes — When to Use Each

The bot has 3 modes: Normal (everyday ICT setups, 7/10 required), Sniper (swing trades, 8/10 required, larger RR), Aggressive (scalps, 3/10 required, fast in/out). Auto mode switches based on ATR.

📊 Normal Mode (Recommended for most users):
• Min confluence: 7/10
• RR: 1:3
• SL buffer: 15 points past OB
• Trades last 10 minutes to 4 hours
• Kill zone required: YES
• Best for: consistent daily trading, accounts over R5,000

🎯 Sniper Mode (Experienced traders):
• Min confluence: 8/10
• RR: 1:5
• SL buffer: 35 points past OB
• Trades last 1–5 days
• Kill zone required: YES
• Fewer trades but much higher quality
• Best for: swing traders, larger accounts, lower time commitment

⚡ Aggressive Mode (Advanced only):
• Min confluence: 3/10
• RR: 1:2
• SL buffer: 5 points past OB
• Trades last 1–15 minutes
• Kill zone NOT required
• WARNING: Higher drawdown periods. Only use with strict DD limits.
• Best for: experienced scalpers who understand risk

🔄 Auto Mode (v8.0 feature):
The bot now automatically switches modes based on ATR (Average True Range):
• ATR > 8: switches to Sniper (high volatility — be selective)
• ATR < 3: switches to Normal (ranging market — standard setups)
• ATR 3–8: stays on your chosen mode
Auto mode resets daily at midnight UTC. Use /mode in Telegram to override.

₿ Bitcoin (BTC) — ICT in Crypto

BTC trades 24/7 including weekends. It respects ICT concepts well but operates on crypto-specific rhythms: US market open (9:30 AM ET), options expiry Fridays, and weekend thin liquidity sweeps.

BTC ICT Key Differences vs Gold:
• No DXY correlation — BTC is driven by risk-on/risk-off sentiment and crypto flows
• Wider spreads — XM BTCUSD# spreads of 5–15 points are normal
• Weekend gaps — BTC can gap significantly Sunday night when TradFi reopens
• 24/7 trading — liquidity sweeps happen at all hours, not just sessions
• Higher ATR — expect 150–400 point daily ranges vs Gold's 15–30 points

BTC Kill Zones (ICT adapted):
• NY Open (9:30–11:00 AM ET / 13:30–15:00 UTC) — Most reliable for BTC. This is when institutional crypto desks come online alongside equity traders.
• Midnight UTC — BTC often runs liquidity at midnight UTC when daily candle closes
• Weekend sweeps — Saturday 00:00–06:00 UTC: thin order books, sweeps then reverse

BTC-Specific Setups:
1. Weekend liquidity grab: BTC sweeps below Friday lows on Saturday, then rallies Sunday/Monday when TradFi opens with positive sentiment
2. NY correlation: When S&P500 opens strong, BTC often follows within 15–30 minutes — use this for NY entries
3. Bitcoin-specific FVGs: BTC FVGs on the 1H chart fill within 48 hours over 70% of the time — much higher rate than Gold
4. Equal highs as magnets: BTC retail traders are very predictable about stop placement — equal highs/lows are hunted religiously

Bot Adaptations for BTC:
• SL minimum: 50pts (vs 0.30pts Gold)
• Trail activates at 1.5× ATR (vs 1.0× for Gold) — BTC retraces violently before continuing
• Break-even offset: 10pts (vs 0.10pts Gold)
• No DXY filter applied
• Weekend trading enabled — bot continues scanning on Saturday/Sunday
• Spread limit: 8pts (5pts is normal, above 8 = unusual)

📈 Nasdaq 100 (NAS100) — ICT on US Tech

NAS100 is the most institutionally driven index. The first hour of the US market (9:30–10:30 AM ET) is the most important ICT window. It follows the Power of 3 almost perfectly every day.

Why NAS100 Respects ICT:
NAS100 is dominated by about 10 massive stocks (Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, etc.). When these institutions buy or sell, they use the same algorithmic order flow described by ICT — they need liquidity, they create FVGs, they leave Order Blocks. The index as a whole reflects this.

NAS100 Daily Pattern (almost every day):
1. Pre-market (13:00–13:30 UTC): Price consolidates from overnight session
2. Market Open (13:30 UTC / 9:30 ET): Judas Swing — false move in wrong direction, sweeping pre-market lows or highs
3. First Hour (13:30–14:30 UTC): Real direction emerges after Judas Swing. This is the highest-probability NAS entry window.
4. Midday (14:30–16:00 UTC): Trending move in real direction, second entry opportunities at FVG retests
5. Close (19:00–21:00 UTC): Late-day profit-taking often creates reversals

NAS100-Specific Zones:
• Previous Day High/Low: NAS PDH/PDL are hunted daily — the most reliable liquidity magnets
• 4H FVGs: NAS100 4-hour FVGs fill within 48h over 65% of the time
• Opening Gap (NDOG): If NAS100 gaps at the open, that gap fills within the same session 72% of the time
• Equal Highs/Lows: Like Gold, retail traders cluster stops at obvious equal levels — institutions hunt these

NAS100 News Events (affect the bot):
• FOMC decisions: 3:00 PM ET — major volatility, bot blocks trading
• NFP: First Friday 8:30 AM ET — NAS often rallies or crashes 150+ points
• CPI/PPI: Monthly inflation reports — NAS is very sensitive to rate expectations
• FOMC minutes: 3-4x/year — similar to FOMC decisions

🔁 Inverse FVG (IFVG) — The Hidden Zone

When a Fair Value Gap gets fully filled, it doesn't just disappear. It flips polarity — becoming an Inverse FVG (IFVG). A bullish FVG that fills now acts as resistance. A bearish FVG that fills now acts as support. These are extremely high-probability zones.

Why IFVGs Work:
When a bullish FVG fills, the traders who bought at the FVG (expecting support) are now at or below their entry. If price returns to that level, they will sell to cut losses OR the institutions who sold to fill the FVG are now defending that level as resistance. Both effects create selling pressure at the IFVG.

IFVG Trading Rules:
1. A bullish FVG that fully fills → becomes a bearish IFVG (resistance zone)
2. A bearish FVG that fully fills → becomes a bullish IFVG (support zone)
3. The IFVG zone = the original FVG boundaries
4. Entry: at the IFVG zone boundary, targeting the opposite side
5. Stop: beyond the IFVG (if price breaks through, the flip failed)

IFVG Strength Factors:
• Age: IFVGs formed within the last 10 candles are strongest (fresh flip)
• Higher timeframe: 4H IFVGs are far stronger than 15m IFVGs
• Multiple touches: an IFVG that holds on first retest becomes even stronger
• HTF alignment: IFVG in direction of H4 bias = elite confluence

The Bot Now Detects IFVGs:
IFVGs appear in the ICT Checklist tab and add +1 to your confluence score when price is approaching one. They are also added to the zone finder in buildSignal — the bot will use an IFVG as an entry zone if no FVG or OB is present.

Visual Tip: On your chart, draw the original FVG zone. When price fills it, change the box to the opposite color. That's your IFVG — watch for price to reject it on the next approach.

📅 Previous Day High/Low (PDH/PDL)

PDH and PDL are the single most important daily levels in ICT. Every professional trader watches them. They represent yesterday's highest and lowest prices — the boundaries that define today's directional bias and the most likely liquidity targets.

Why PDH/PDL Matter:
Every day, retail traders who bought near PDH (previous day high) have their stops just above it. Retail sellers who shorted near PDL have stops just below it. This creates two massive liquidity pools — one above PDH, one below PDL — that institutions target daily.

How ICT Traders Use PDH/PDL:
• Bullish day: PDL gets swept first (Judas Swing down), then price targets PDH and beyond
• Bearish day: PDH gets swept first (Judas Swing up), then price targets PDL and below
• Range day: Price trades between PDL and PDH all day, fading the extremes

Entry model using PDH/PDL:
1. Wait for price to sweep PDL (wick below, then close back above)
2. Look for FVG or OB immediately above PDL
3. Enter long at that zone, targeting PDH
4. Reverse for shorts using PDH sweep

Weekly Open is even more powerful:
The Monday market open price is THE most important weekly level. ICT traders use it to determine the weekly bias:
• Price above weekly open = bullish weekly bias
• Price below weekly open = bearish weekly bias
The bot now tracks the weekly open and factors it into zone quality scoring.

Midnight Open (00:00 UTC and 05:00 UTC):
• The 00:00 UTC candle open is significant for all markets
• The 05:00 UTC (New York midnight = 00:00 EST) is ICT's most watched daily level
• Price frequently returns to the midnight open during the trading day
• The bot now tracks both and adds +1 to score when price is near these levels

📊 ADX — Measuring Trend Strength

ADX (Average Directional Index) tells you HOW STRONG a trend is, not which direction. An ADX above 25 means a strong trend — ICT setups in trending markets have much higher win rates than the same setups in ranging markets.

ADX Readings and What They Mean:
• ADX below 18: Ranging/choppy market — avoid directional ICT setups. FVG retests in ranges often fail.
• ADX 18–25: Weak trend developing — normal setups okay, keep lot size conservative
• ADX 25–40: Strong trend — this is the ideal ICT trading environment. FVGs, OBs, and MSS signals have highest win rates here.
• ADX above 40: Very strong trend — momentum continuation setups work well, but reversals are risky
• ADX above 60: Extreme trend — these are rare; reduce size as volatility risk is high

How the Bot Uses ADX:
• ADX below 18 = -1 to confluence score (ranging markets punished)
• ADX 18–25 = no change
• ADX 25+ = trending confirmed, contributes to session card indicator
• The ADX value shows live in the ICT checklist tab and today's session card
• 🔥 icon = strong trend (ADX 25+) | 📈 = trending | 😴 = ranging

Why Not Just Trade All the Time?
Ranging markets are where ICT strategies lose money. In a range, FVGs form and fill immediately in both directions. Order Blocks get violated constantly. The same setup that works beautifully in a trend produces losing trades in a range. ADX filters out the noise.

Gold Typical ADX:
• During London kill zone: often 25–45 (strong trend periods)
• Asian session: often 10–18 (ranging — bot avoids this)
• Post-NFP/FOMC: can spike above 50

BTC Typical ADX:
• During weekend: often 10–20 (low trend strength)
• During major moves: 35–60
• After big news: can exceed 70

📓 Trade Journal — Your Unfair Advantage

The Trade Journal tab (📓) auto-logs every signal evaluation — including rejections. This tells you exactly why the bot is or isn't trading, and which filters are blocking the most setups.

What the Journal Tracks:
• Every signal evaluated (every 60 seconds when bot is running)
• Score at time of evaluation (out of 12)
• Why a signal was rejected (score too low / no KZ / bias conflict / P&D filter / no zone)
• ADX and ATR at time of evaluation
• Whether key levels (PDH/PDL/IFVG/Triple Zone) were present
• Trade details when a trade IS placed

The Rejection Analysis Chart:
Shows your most common rejection reasons with percentages. If you see:
• "Score X/12 < min Y" 80% of the time → lower your minScore by 1, or switch mode
• "No kill zone" 60% → you might be running the bot outside your sessions
• "No entry zone" 40% → FVG/OB detection needs more candles (use Normal mode more)
• "HTF bias conflict" → market is ranging/neutral at H4 level
• "News block" → lots of high-impact events (check economic calendar)

Best Setup Today Card:
Shows the highest-scoring setup of the day, even if it was rejected. If you see a 9/12 setup getting rejected by "No Kill Zone", that tells you exactly when to be watching the chart manually.

How to Use the Journal to Improve:
1. Check it daily — what was the average score? If consistently 4–5, your market structure is ranging
2. If "Score X < min Y" is your top rejection reason, try lowering min score by 1 for one week and track results in History
3. If "No entry zone" is top rejection, try Aggressive mode which allows displacement entries
4. Match your rejection reasons to the time of day — if 80% of rejections happen 07:00–13:00 UTC, your ideal trading window is different from what you think

🛡️ Break-Even, Trailing & Partial Close

The bot's three-stage trade management system: partial close at 1:1, break-even at 1:1 profit, trailing stop that follows price. These three combined turn a 50% win rate system into a profitable one.

Stage 1: Partial Close at 1:1 RR
When trade profit equals the initial risk (1:1), the bot closes 50% of the position. This books real profit while leaving a runner for the full target.
• Gold: fires at 1× SL distance in profit
• BTC/NAS: fires at exactly 1× SL distance (more conservative due to volatility)
• Effect: Turns a 50% win rate into positive expectancy even with 1:1 exits

Stage 2: Break-Even Stop
After partial close fires, the stop loss is moved to entry price + offset:
• Gold: entry + 0.10pts (covers spread)
• NAS100: entry + 5pts
• BTC: entry + 10pts
• Effect: Trade can no longer lose money after break-even triggers. This is the key to surviving drawdown periods.

Stage 3: Trailing Stop
After the break-even level is reached and price continues moving in your favour, a trailing stop activates:
• Trail activates at: 1.5× ATR profit (BTC/NAS) or 1.0× ATR (Gold)
• Trail distance: 1.2× ATR (BTC/NAS) or 0.8× ATR (Gold)
• Minimum: Gold 0.30pts, NAS 20pts, BTC 50pts
• Effect: Locks in growing profits as the trade runs, while giving room for normal price movement

The Math of These Three Combined:
Say you enter 0.02 lots with a 30pt SL on Gold:
• Partial close at 30pt profit: 0.01 lot closed → +R3 locked in
• Remaining 0.01 lot now has break-even stop (worst case: +R0)
• Trade can only make money from here on
• Even if the runner hits SL at break-even, total trade = +R3 (win)
• Only a true reversal below entry costs you (but maximum = break-even stop)
This is why the bot's win-rate in R terms is much higher than in trade count terms.

🔢 The 12-Point Scoring System (Updated)

The bot now scores setups out of 12 (expanded from 10). Two new factors: ADX trend strength and IFVG/PDH/PDL key level proximity. This gives the scoring system much finer precision for filtering high-quality vs low-quality setups.

The 12-Point Confluence System:

1️⃣ Kill Zone (Prime) — London for Gold, NY for BTC/NAS → +2
2️⃣ Kill Zone (Secondary) → +1
3️⃣ Silver Bullet window (ultra-specific window) → +2 bonus
4️⃣ FVG approaching + quality ≥ 4 → +2 | FVG quality ≥ 2 → +1
5️⃣ OB in zone + quality ≥ 4 → +2 | OB quality ≥ 2 → +1
6️⃣ Triple Confluence (FVG + OB at same level) → +1 bonus
7️⃣ Market Structure Shift (BOS/CHoCH, candle close confirmed) → +1
8️⃣ Liquidity Sweep (Rule #1) → +1
9️⃣ HTF Bias aligned (H4 EMA) → +1
🔟 Full MTF alignment (H4 + H1 + M15 all agree) → +1
1️⃣1️⃣ OTE (61.8–79% Fib) + P/D correct → +2 | one of two → +1
1️⃣2️⃣ Power of 3 / Judas Swing confirmed → +1

New Bonus Factors:
🆕 IFVG (Inverse FVG in zone) → +1
🆕 Key Level proximity (PDH/PDL/Weekly Open/Midnight Open) → +1

Deductions:
• DXY conflict (Gold/Forex only) → -1
• ADX below 18 (ranging market) → -1
• Wide spread → -1

Mode Thresholds (vs new 12-point system):
• Aggressive: 3/12 minimum
• Normal: 7/12 minimum
• Sniper: 9/12 minimum (raised from 8 due to expanded scoring)

Why this matters: An 11/12 setup is rare — maybe 2–3 times per week. But when it appears, win rates are exceptional. The extra precision of IFVG and key level scoring separates genuinely elite setups from good-but-not-great ones.

⚡ Speed Optimizations — Why the Bot Is Faster

Several technical improvements make the bot respond faster to market conditions: self-healing price feed, immediate recovery on app resume, non-blocking H4 candle fetch, and symbol-aware analysis that avoids wasteful checks.

Key Speed Improvements:

1. Self-healing price feed: If the bot detects a stale price (>60 seconds old), it immediately triggers a fresh fetch AND logs the issue rather than silently pausing trade management. Recovery happens in the next analysis cycle (60 seconds) instead of waiting for a manual restart.

2. App resume — instant refresh: When you switch back to the app after the phone backgrounds it, the bot immediately calls fetchPrice() before waiting for the next analysis cycle. Previously it could take up to 60 seconds to update after you opened the app.

3. Non-blocking H4 fetch: H4 candles for bias calculation are fetched in the background (.catch(() => {})) so they never delay the main analysis cycle. If H4 is unavailable, the bot falls back to H1 EMA automatically.

4. NDOG/FVG/OB minimum size filters: Detection functions now skip candles below the minimum significant size for each instrument (ATR-relative). This prevents the engine from building up large arrays of noise FVGs that then have to be sorted — much faster on instruments with high point counts like BTC.

5. 60s cooldown between trades: The main loop runs every 60 seconds but has mode-specific cooldowns (30s Aggressive, 2min Normal, 5min Sniper) that short-circuit before running the full analysis — saving CPU on mobile when no trade is possible anyway.

6. Journal rendering batched: The journal only re-renders when new entries arrive, not on every analysis cycle. The rejection chart uses sorted percentages so it scales to 50+ entries without slowdown.

🎯 Sniper Mode — When to Use It

Sniper mode requires 9/12 confluence and only enters in Silver Bullet windows. It may only fire 2–3 times per week — but those trades have elite win rates when all conditions align. It is NOT for impatient traders.

Sniper Mode Requirements (all must be true):
• Score ≥ 9/12
• Kill Zone active (Prime session for your symbol)
• Silver Bullet window preferred
• Full 3-timeframe alignment (H4 + H1 + M15)
• Liquidity sweep confirmed
• FVG or OB in direction (quality ≥ 3)
• P/D zone correct (discount for buys, premium for sells)

Sniper Trade Parameters:
• SL buffer: 200pts (BTC), 20pts (NAS), 35pts (Gold) — wide enough to survive retracement
• RR: 1:5 minimum (London/NY bonus: 1:5.5)
• Partial close: 50% at 1:1, runner to 1:5
• Trail activates: 1.5× ATR in profit
• No aggressive entries — must have clear zone

How Often Sniper Fires:
• Gold: 2–4 times per week in ideal conditions
• BTC: 3–5 times per week (trades weekends)
• NAS100: 2–3 times per week during NY session
• During ranging (ADX < 20): may not fire for 2–3 days in a row

Patience is the Edge:
The average Sniper setup has approximately:
• 68–72% win rate (based on ICT methodology backtest data)
• 1:5 average RR when hit
• Expectancy: 0.68×5 - 0.32×1 = 3.40 - 0.32 = 3.08R per trade
Even ONE Sniper trade per week at 3R = 12R per month on the account

When NOT to use Sniper:
• When ADX is below 20 (ranging — Sniper will almost never fire)
• During major news week (FOMC, NFP, CPI) — use Normal or stop
• On Friday afternoon — gap risk means SL hits are more likely overnight

💹 Multi-Symbol Strategy — Gold + BTC + NAS100

Running the bot on multiple symbols is powerful but requires understanding each instrument's rhythm. Don't run all three at the same time on a small account — the correlations and risk overlap can compound drawdowns.

Correlations to Know:
• Gold ↕ DXY: Inverse — when dollar strengthens, Gold falls (80% correlation)
• NAS100 ↕ DXY: Inverse (weak) — dollar strength hurts US tech exports
• NAS100 ↕ BTC: Positive (moderate) — risk-on sentiment lifts both
• Gold ↕ BTC: Positive (weak) — both are "store of value" plays
• Risk-off (fear) events: Gold rises, BTC falls, NAS falls
• Risk-on (greed) events: Gold flat/falls, BTC rises, NAS rises

Best Multi-Symbol Approach (small account):
Recommended: run ONE symbol at a time. Switch between them based on what session is active:
• 07:00–10:00 UTC: Switch to GOLD# (London kill zone — Gold's prime time)
• 13:00–16:00 UTC: Switch to NAS100# (NY open — NAS prime time)
• Weekend: Switch to BTCUSD# (only market open)

If Running Multiple Simultaneously (medium+ account):
• Reduce risk per trade (halve your risk% if running 2 symbols, third it for 3 symbols)
• Max 1 open trade per symbol simultaneously
• Monitor total exposure in Risk Dashboard — keep under 5% account
• Avoid opposite trades (long Gold + short NAS during same risk-off move = good hedge, but confirm first)

Symbol Settings Cheat Sheet:
| Symbol | Best Hours | Min Score | SL Buffer | Spread Max |
| GOLD# | 07–10, 13–16 UTC | 7/12 | 15pts | 0.8pts |
| NAS100# | 13–17 UTC | 7/12 | 50pts | 5pts |
| BTCUSD# | 13–16 UTC (+wknd) | 7/12 | 100pts | 8pts |
